evidence: Chez Damier worked A&R for Kevin Saunderson's KMS Records during its early years and released his own single, 'Can You Feel It,' on the label in 1992. Documented in fabric London's KMS retrospective, Discogs' release data for 'Can You Feel It,' and KMS's own label record on this map, which already names Damier among the artists the label developed.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: 'Big Fun' is KMS's commercial peak, pop-facing house built to cross over. 'Can You Feel It,' made by the label's own A&R four years later, is rawer and more interior, closer to the deep house Damier and Ron Trent would build Prescription Records around the next year.

explanation: Chez Damier worked for Kevin Saunderson's label, KMS, helping find and sign artists, and put out his own record there in 1992 before starting his own label the following year. KMS gave him a working studio and a way to release records, the way Transmat did for Carl Craig, but from inside the label rather than as an outside signing: his job put him in the room for the label's decisions before he made a record of his own there.
